workflowArticle.title: Review node_modules and build caches before reclaiming Mac storage
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Decide which generated project artifacts are rebuildable before using tiered cleanup, then check whether growth returns.
workflowArticle.audience: Apple Silicon Mac developers investigating project/build-cache growth; not a Windows replacement article.
workflowArticle.distinctMechanism: Use DriveScape risk-tiered staging and scan snapshots to distinguish project outputs, shared package stores and potentially irreplaceable Docker/virtual-environment data. Contrast Breathing Room owner/project views and ongoing investigation without claiming it implements the same sunburst or duplicate engine.
workflowArticle.proposedLead: Start by separating rebuildable project outputs from shared stores and original data. DriveScape documents a tiered, review-first workflow; labels and file sizes do not establish that a folder is disposable.
sections: Locate a heavy project with a disk map; numbers in vendor demos are examples, not our results.
Classify project output versus shared store versus original data; check manifests, backups and rebuild/download cost.
Review exact locations and Trash versus permanent-delete behavior; do not execute cleanup for article research.
Re-scan to compare snapshots; history is not writer attribution.
Choose one-off visual cleanup or continuing app/activity investigation; disclose Breathing Room affiliation and preview/hosted caveats.
visualPlacement: Cleared real DriveScape app UI immediately after lead; currently blocked.
Selected Breathing Room Space browser preview later, with example/native disclosure.
workflowArticle.interactionPass: Hand off a local checklist/decision aid: manifest present? backup? rebuild cost? shared store/volume? Answer unknown routes to review, never automatic deletion. No filesystem access or invented size estimates.
